s:
Which of the following statements regarding Nannaya Bhattu are correct?
I. Nannaya Bhattu was a Telugu poet and the author of 'Andhra Mahabharatam', a Telugu retelling of the Sanskrit-language Mahabharata.
II. He is also credited with writing the Andhra Shabda Chintamani, a Sanskrit treatise on Telugu grammar.
III. Raja Raja Narendra donated an Agrahara to Nannaya
x:
Statement I: Correct. Nannaya Bhattu, popularly known as Adi Kavi, was the first great Telugu poet. He began translating the Mahabharata into Telugu under the patronage of Eastern Chalukya king Raja Raja Narendra. He translated the Adi Parva, Sabha Parva, and a portion of the Aranya Parva. Statement II: Correct. Nannaya is traditionally credited with writing Andhra Shabda Chintamani, the earliest known Sanskrit treatise on Telugu grammar. Although the original work is no longer available, later scholars have frequently referred to it. Statement III: Correct. An inscription records that Raja Raja Narendra granted Nandampudi Agrahara to Nannaya in recognition of his literary scholarship and service. Since all three statements are correct, the answer is
Option (4).
n: Nannaya – Adi Kavi of Telugu literature
Mahabharata Trio (Kavitrayam) – Nannaya, Tikkana and Errana

s: What was the official language of the Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi?
x:
The official language used in the inscriptions and administration of the Eastern Chalukyas was Sanskrit, especially during the early phase of their rule. However, the dynasty played a decisive role in the development of Telugu language and literature, particularly under Rajaraja Narendra, who patronized Nannaya, the first Telugu poet.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (1).

s: Ayyana Mahadevi built the Jain temple 'Nedumba Vasati' near Vijayawada. She was the queen of
x:
Ayyana Mahadevi was one of the queens of Gunaga Vijayaditya III, one of the greatest rulers of the Eastern Chalukya dynasty. She was a devout follower of Jainism and constructed the famous Nedumba Vasati, a Jain temple near present-day Vijayawada. Although the Eastern Chalukya rulers were predominantly patrons of Hinduism, they also extended generous patronage to Jainism and Buddhism, reflecting the religious tolerance that existed during their rule. The construction of Nedumba Vasati is an important example of Jain patronage under the Eastern Chalukyas. Why the other options are incorrect:
Option (2): Jatachodabheema – Belonged to the Telugu Choda dynasty and had no association with Ayyana Mahadevi or Nedumba Vasati.
Option (3): Kubja Vishnuvardhana – Founder of the Eastern Chalukya dynasty, but Ayyana Mahadevi was not his queen.
Option (4): Jayasimha Vallabha – An Eastern Chalukya ruler, but there is no historical evidence connecting him with the construction of Nedumba Vasati.
n: Gunaga Vijayaditya III – One of the greatest Eastern Chalukya rulers
Famous Monument – Nedumba Vasati (Jain Temple) near Vijayawada

Which of the following poets is known as “Abhinava Nannaya”?
x:
Viswanatha Satyanarayana is popularly honoured with the title "Abhinava Nannaya" because of his extraordinary contribution to Telugu literature and his mastery over classical Telugu language, comparable to that of Nannaya Bhattu, the Adi Kavi of Telugu. He authored more than one hundred literary works covering poetry, novels, dramas, essays and philosophical writings. His monumental work Ramayana Kalpavriksham earned him the Jnanpith Award, making him the first Telugu writer to receive India's highest literary honour. Rayaprolu Subbarao is regarded as one of the pioneers of modern romantic poetry in Telugu, Sri Sri revolutionized progressive poetry through Mahaprasthanam, and Boyi Bheemanna was an eminent Dalit poet and social reformer. None of them is known by the title "Abhinava Nannaya."
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (1).

Which Vishnukundin ruler had transferred the capital from Amarapuri to Denduluru? Se
x:
The Vishnukundins emerged as an important dynasty in the Deccan after the decline of the Ikshvakus and the Salankayanas. Their early capital was Amarapuri (identified with Amaravati region). As the kingdom expanded towards the coastal Andhra region, Madhavavarma II shifted the capital to Denduluru (near present-day Eluru in West Godavari district). This strategic shift enabled better control over the fertile Vengi region and facilitated administration of the eastern coastal territories. Madhavavarma II was the most powerful ruler of the dynasty. He assumed the title Janasraya, performed several Vedic sacrifices such as the Ashvamedha, and greatly expanded the kingdom. Why the other options are incorrect:
Option (1): Vikramendravarma – He was an important Vishnukundin ruler but is not credited with shifting the capital to Denduluru.
Option (3): Govindavarma – Founder of the Vishnukundin dynasty. During his reign, the capital remained at Amarapuri.
Option (4): Manchana Bhattaraka – A later ruler who ruled during the declining phase of the dynasty and did not shift the capital.

s: Undavally caves are associated with =) (
x:
The Undavalli Caves, situated near Vijayawada on the banks of the Krishna River, are among the finest examples of rock-cut architecture in Andhra Pradesh. These caves were excavated during the Vishnukundin period (5th–6th Century CE). Although they were originally developed as Buddhist monastic caves, they were later converted into Hindu cave temples. The most striking feature of the caves is the monolithic reclining image of Lord Vishnu (Anantasayana Vishnu) carved from a single block of granite. The caves consist of four storeys, displaying remarkable rock-cut architectural skill and reflecting the transition from Buddhist to Hindu religious traditions.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (1).

s: The Chalukya king who is said to have built 108 Saiva temples on the name of Narendra Mrigeswara was
x:
Vijayaditya II is traditionally credited with constructing 108 Shiva temples, known as Narendra Mrigeswaralayas, to commemorate his military victories. This earned him a distinguished place among the temple-building rulers of the Eastern Chalukya dynasty.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (2).

s: What is the evidence that Narayanabhattu helped Nannayabhattu in the process of translation of Mahabharata?
x:
The Nandampudi Donation Inscription is the primary historical evidence showing that Narayanabhattu assisted Nannaya Bhattu in translating the Mahabharata into Telugu. The inscription records that Rajaraja Narendra granted the village of Nandampudi as an agrahara in recognition of the literary services rendered by Narayanabhattu. It also acknowledges his scholarly assistance to Nannaya during the translation of the Mahabharata. This inscription is therefore an important source for understanding the collaborative efforts behind the earliest Telugu Mahabharata and the literary patronage extended by the Eastern Chalukya rulers.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (1).
n: Importance – Confirms Narayanabhattu's assistance to Nannaya

s: Which Chalukya king is said to have built 108 Shaivalayas?
x:
Vijayaditya II, an important ruler of the Eastern Chalukya dynasty, is traditionally credited with constructing 108 Shiva temples (Shaivalayas). According to historical tradition, these temples were built to commemorate his military victories and his deep devotion to Lord Shiva. His reign witnessed the growth of Shaivism and the construction of several temples, contributing significantly to the religious and architectural development of the Vengi kingdom. This tradition occupies an important place in the history of the Eastern Chalukyas and is frequently asked in APPSC examinations.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (3).

s: During the period of Chalukyas who received the title "Gandharva Vidya Visharada"?
x:
Chellavva, an accomplished female musician during the Eastern Chalukya period, was honoured with the title "Gandharva Vidya Visharada", meaning "one who is highly proficient in the art of music." The title reflects the importance given to music and performing arts under the Eastern Chalukyas. Historical inscriptions indicate that women also occupied an important position in the cultural life of the kingdom and received royal recognition for their artistic excellence.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (4).

s: The Chalukya King who developed Kandukuru as Bejawada?
x:
Vijayaditya III, one of the prominent rulers of the Eastern Chalukya dynasty, is credited with developing Kandukuru and strengthening its administrative importance. Historical records associate his reign with the development of urban centres and the consolidation of Chalukya authority in the Vengi region. His rule witnessed political stability, economic prosperity and encouragement to temple construction and literature.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (3).

s: Who authored the medical treatise "Kalyanakaraka"?
x:
Kalyanakaraka is a celebrated medical treatise (Ayurvedic work) written by the Jain scholar Ugradityacharya. The text deals with various aspects of medicine, including diagnosis, treatment of diseases, diet, preventive healthcare and medicinal preparations. It is regarded as one of the important contributions of Jain scholars to the development of Indian medical science.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (3).

s: Who was the Eastern Chalukya king who issued the Inscription of Vipparla?
x:
The Vipparla Inscription was issued during the reign of Jayasimha Vallabha, an early ruler of the Eastern Chalukya dynasty. The inscription is an important historical source for understanding the administrative organization, land grants and political expansion of the Eastern Chalukyas in the Vengi region. It also throws light on the consolidation of Chalukya authority in Andhra Pradesh.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (3).

s: Gunaga Vijayaditya assumed the title "Tripura-Martya-Mahesvara" to mark the victory over which cities?
x:
Gunaga Vijayaditya, one of the greatest rulers of the Eastern Chalukyas, assumed the title "Tripura-Martya-Mahesvara" after achieving victories over Kiranapuram, Achalapuram and Kandukur. The title symbolizes his conquest of these three fortified cities and reflects his military achievements and expansion of the Eastern Chalukya kingdom.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (4).

s: Who bears the title "Kollabhiganda"?
x:
Chalukya Bhima I, one of the prominent rulers of the Eastern Chalukya dynasty, bore the title "Kollabhiganda." He is remembered for strengthening the kingdom, encouraging temple construction and building the famous Bhimeswara Temple at Draksharama, one of the Pancharama Kshetras. His reign marked an important phase in the political and cultural history of the Eastern Chalukyas.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (3).

s: Chalukya mathematician Pavuluri Mallana's Agraharam?
x:
Pavuluri Mallana, the celebrated mathematician of the Eastern Chalukya period, belonged to Kaluchumbarru Agraharam. He translated Mahaviracharya's Ganitasarasangraha into Telugu, making mathematical knowledge accessible to Telugu scholars. His contribution occupies an important place in the history of mathematics in Andhra.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (4).

s: Who was the greatest king of the Eastern Chalukyas?
x:
Gunaga Vijayaditya (Vijayaditya III) is widely regarded as the greatest ruler of the Eastern Chalukya dynasty. He greatly expanded the kingdom, defeated several neighbouring rulers and assumed prestigious titles such as Tripura-Martya- Mahesvara. His reign marked the political and military zenith of the Eastern Chalukyas.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (4).
n: Greatest Eastern Chalukya Ruler – Gunaga Vijayaditya

s: Who patronized Nannaya Bhattu?
x:
Nannaya Bhattu, the Adi Kavi of Telugu, was patronized by Rajaraja Narendra, the Eastern Chalukya ruler. At the king's request, Nannaya began translating the Mahabharata into Telugu, laying the foundation of classical Telugu literature.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (1).

s: Who was the first king of the Chalukya-Chola line?
x:
Kulothunga I, originally known as Rajendra Chalukya, was the first ruler of the Chalukya-Chola dynasty. He united the Eastern Chalukya Kingdom of Vengi with the Chola Empire, giving rise to the Chalukya-Chola line. His reign marked an important phase in the political history of South India.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (3).

s: "Samastha Gandharva Vidya Kovida" Chellava was the court singer of whom?
x:
Chellava, who bore the title "Samastha Gandharva Vidya Kovida", was the celebrated court singer of Chalukya Bhima I of the Eastern Chalukya dynasty. The title reflects her extraordinary mastery over music and indicates the importance given to performing arts during the Eastern Chalukya period.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (2).

s: Rajamahendri (present-day Rajahmundry) was developed under which dynasty?
x:
Rajamahendravaram (Rajahmundry) was developed as an important capital by the Eastern Chalukyas, particularly during the reign of Rajaraja Narendra. The city became an important centre of Telugu culture and literature. It was in Rajamahendravaram that Nannaya Bhattaraka, the Adi Kavi of Telugu, began translating the Mahabharata into Telugu under the patronage of Rajaraja Narendra. Because of this literary and political importance, Rajamahendravaram occupies a special place in the history of Andhra Pradesh.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (4).

s: Rajamahendri (present-day Rajahmundry) was built during whose reign?
x:
Rajamahendravaram (Rajahmundry) was developed as an important political and cultural centre by the Eastern Chalukyas, especially during the reign of Rajaraja Narendra. The city became famous as: • The capital of the Eastern Chalukyas. • The place where Nannaya Bhattaraka, the Adi Kavi of Telugu, began translating the Mahabharata into Telugu. • An important centre of Telugu literature and culture.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (4).

Vijayanagara Kings represent a dynasty, not a pilgrimage centre. 12. Who was mainly responsible for introducing the Ryotwari System in the Madras Presidency? 1. Elphinstone 2. Thomas Munro 3. Mc. Cord Nee 4. John Lawrence Answer: (2) Thomas Munro Explanation: The Ryotwari System was introduced in the Madras Presidency by Sir Thomas Munro during the early nineteenth century. Under this system, the government collected land revenue directly from individual cultivators (Ryots) instead of through Zamindars or intermediaries. Every ryot was recognized as the proprietor of his land, provided he regularly paid the land revenue fixed by the government. The system was first experimented with in parts of South India and later became the principal land revenue system in the Madras Presidency. It aimed to eliminate intermediaries, but in practice the heavy land tax often placed a severe burden on cultivators. Hence, the correct answer is Option (2). Exam Note:
Direct settlement between Government and Ryot

Introduced mainly in Madras Presidency 13. What is known as the 'Athens of Vijayanagara'? 1. Present Nellore and Chittoor districts 2. Present Bangalore, Kolar and Chittoor districts 3. Pandya regions 4. Valley areas around Virupaksha Temple Answer: (2) Present Bangalore, Kolar and Chittoor districts Explanation: The region comprising the present-day Bangalore, Kolar and Chittoor districts was popularly called the "Athens of Vijayanagara" because it emerged as an outstanding centre of education, literature, philosophy, art and culture during the Vijayanagara period. The rulers of Vijayanagara encouraged scholars, poets, musicians and philosophers by granting them land, honours and patronage. Numerous educational institutions, temples and literary centres flourished in this region, making it comparable to Athens, the famous ancient centre of learning in Greece. Hence, the correct answer is Option (2). Exam Note:

Famous for → Learning, literature and culture 14. Which of the following temples in Andhra Pradesh is the only temple with two flagpoles? 1. Tirumala – Sri Venkateswara Swamy Temple 2. Simhachalam – Sri Narasimha Swamy Temple 3. Yadagirigutta – Sri Lakshminarasimha Swamy Temple 4. Sri Kurma – Sri Kurmanatha Temple Answer: (4) Sri Kurma – Sri Kurmanatha Temple Explanation: The Sri Kurmanatha Temple at Srikurmam in Srikakulam district is unique because it is the only temple in Andhra Pradesh with two Dhwaja Stambhas (flagpoles). The temple is dedicated to Lord Kurma, the second incarnation (Kurma Avatar) of Lord Vishnu, and is one of the very few temples in the world exclusively dedicated to this avatar. Built mainly during the Eastern Ganga period, the temple is renowned for its distinctive architecture, rich sculptures and importance in the Vaishnavite tradition. The presence of two flagpoles is one of its most distinctive architectural features, making it a favourite question in APPSC examinations. Hence, the correct answer is Option (4). Exam Note:
Only temple with two flagpoles in Andhra Pradesh → Sri Kurmanatha Temple, Srikurmam
Dedicated to → Lord Kurma (Second Avatar of Vishnu)
